headline: Enjoy Truncated Moorland and Dark Sky Access
reservation: Entry to Exmoor National Park is generally free, though specific parking permits for National Park Authority lots can be purchased via their online shop. Accommodation varies from quaint villages to remote camping; systems operate independently and require direct official confirmation. Dark Sky events, particularly during the October festival, often require separate booking.

days.title: Wilderness Coast and Cliffs

stops.name: South West Coast Path
stops.detail: Walk the first stage of the UK's longest National Trail along high sea cliffs and steep-sided gorges.

stops.name: Selworthy Beacon
stops.detail: View the heather in bloom and look out over the Bristol Channel coast.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours; conditions vary on narrow coastal roads.
days.note: Pace your hike for the rugged terrain; the coastline here is the highest on the British mainland.

days.title: Ancient Valleys and History

stops.name: Tarr Steps
stops.detail: Visit this ancient clapper bridge in a wooded valley; check local status following seasonal storm damage.

stops.name: Simonsbath
stops.detail: Explore the high moors and see the source of the River Exe nearby.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; check for livestock on open moorland roads.
days.note: Check official updates for bridge access at Tarr Steps before visiting.

days.title: Beacons and Dark Skies

stops.name: Dunkery Beacon
stops.detail: Ascend the highest point on Exmoor and in Somerset for panoramic regional views.

stops.name: International Dark Sky Reserve
stops.detail: Stay late to witness shooting stars and the Milky Way in Europe's first Dark Sky Reserve.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; evening visibility requires extra caution.
days.note: Golden hour at Dunkery Beacon is season-dependent; prepare for rapid temperature drops.

intel.title: Village and Trailhead Permits
intel.text: Parking permits for Authority-managed sites are available through the official online shop. Many smaller hamlets have limited spaces that fill early during peak summer months.

intel.title: Remote Connectivity
intel.text: Mobile reception is frequently absent in deep wooded valleys and remote moors. Download offline maps or carry official physical guides before entering the former royal hunting forest.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel is available in larger villages like Dulverton and Lynton, but is not found in the high moorland center. Refill at gateway towns before traversing the 693 square kilometer park.

intel.title: Heather and Stargazing
intel.text: Late summer brings blooming heather to Selworthy Beacon, while October is the peak time for organized dark sky activities. Suggested morning starts help avoid peak crowds at popular coastal trailheads.

intel.title: Rights of Way
intel.text: Exmoor features 1000km of rights of way across moorland and farmland. Visitors must respect active farming and managed environment boundaries shaped over thousands of years.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental at Taunton or Tiverton Parkway rail stations. Stock up on supplies in these gateway towns before a 60-minute bus or drive into the park's central hamlets.
plan.vehicle: Smaller cars are best for narrow country lanes; check rental restrictions for steep coastal grades.
plan.goldenHour: Selworthy Beacon offers views of the heather-clad cliffs, best at sunset in late summer.
